assessments.reasoning: The introduction on physical page 19 describes an interactive Lisp system and marks a cross-implementation manual with certain Interlisp-10-specific material. Physical page 21 gives the October 1978 third revision. The earlier title and acknowledgments name the author and Xerox PARC and BBN contributions.

challenge.method: Compare the collective name with PDP-10 deployment and the 1973 predecessor rename. Check the later Interlisp-D overview and the separately named Interlisp-VAX report for a competing language-versus-implementation reading.
challenge.results: The introduction explicitly calls Interlisp-10 the DEC PDP-10 implementation, with machine and host qualifiers. Xerox treats Interlisp itself as a dialect of Lisp in the later overview. The 1978 preface gives a specific rename in a succession of implementations, which supplies no blanket historical identity or compatibility assertion.

limitations: The documentary identity remains specific to the described Interlisp referent. The active registry language entity represents that source language even though the manuals also describe its environment.
